newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Salvadoran president pledges to punish defrauders.
newsitem.headline: Salvadoran president pledges to punish defrauders.

text.p: El Salvador's President Armando Calderon Sol pledged on Sunday to get to the bottom of financial fraud, in which top executives are charged with siphoning about $113.6 million from investment accounts.

The fraud has led to the arrest of four private bank executives, among them top businessman Roberto Mathies Hill. Mathies is owner of Finsepro, the financial firm accused of bilking the local investors.
"I am totally committed to getting to the bottom of the investigation and to punish whoever has done this," Calderon said in a media address.
"Impunity is a stain of the past. The law is equal for all," he added.
Mathies is a member of a business group directly linked to Calderon's Nationalist Republican Alliance (ARENA) and head of the country's football selection committee.
Also jailed were former Financial System Superintendent Rafael Rodriguez and businessman Mario Galdamez.
The scandal gyped 1,400 Salvadorans in the Finsepro financial firm, and "caused profound injury to the economic and social development process," Calderon said.
He promised to "make his best effort to recover the lost property."
